# Phase One — Main Constellation Possibilities

The Awtsmoos creates every doorway anew, yet the home should not become a wall;
Awtsmoos.com can reveal every living app and game while keeping the first glance calm and small.

## User intent translated into missions

- Give the whole product family a simple futuristic visual language: dark luminous surfaces, restrained glass, tiny orbital motion, quick transforms, no decorative clutter.
- Make secondary UI retractable instead of permanently occupying space.
- Expose every legitimate unpublished app and game from the main discovery experience.
- Keep the homepage itself sparse: one launcher/search surface should carry breadth rather than hundreds of visible cards.
- Repair concrete usability problems encountered while validating newly exposed routes.
- Preserve working app/game visual identities unless they are objectively broken.

## Extreme possibility field

1. Main Worlds launcher becomes a searchable constellation containing top-level worlds plus every cataloged app and game.
2. Results grouped into compact retractable sections: Core, Apps, Games, Community/System.
3. Each group can collapse without hiding search matches.
4. Search can match titles, aliases, categories, descriptions, genres, and route names.
5. Cards use one-line title + one-line purpose, no long marketing paragraphs.
6. Hover/focus gives subtle parallax glow, not giant motion.
7. Mobile launcher becomes a bottom-sheet/full-height drawer with sticky search and retractable groups.
8. Reduced-motion users get no spatial movement.
9. Main launcher imports source catalogs instead of duplicating 69+26 records.
10. Catalog completeness can be tested mechanically against every launchable first-level app/game directory.
11. Unpublished-but-real routes can be promoted by adding one catalog record rather than hand-editing homepage markup.
12. Invalid/debug/test/internal routes remain excluded through an explicit publication policy.
13. Apps and Games storefront counts should derive from catalog lengths instead of stale hardcoded numbers.
14. Main homepage can show one compact live count such as “95 tools & worlds” inside the launcher rather than adding visible clutter.
15. Keyboard navigation should cross section boundaries cleanly and Enter opens the selected door.
16. Escape collapses the launcher; slash or G focuses discovery according to existing shortcut patterns.
17. Cards should support pointer, keyboard, touch, and reduced motion uniformly.
18. Current dirty homepage/storefront changes must be preserved, not reset.
19. Newly exposed routes should receive focused smoke checks for viewport, load errors, overflow, and obviously unusable controls.
20. Any broken candidate should be fixed locally; a working unusual UI should remain unusual.

## Five possible architectures

### A — Duplicate everything into `world-catalog.js`
Simple runtime, terrible maintenance, guaranteed catalog drift. Reject.

### B — Homepage imports `PUBLIC_APPS` and `GAMES` directly
Single source of truth, easiest completeness testing, reasonable module graph. Strong candidate.

### C — Generate a build-time merged JSON catalog
Fast runtime and explicit artifact, but adds generation obligations and stale-output risk. Useful only if import graph becomes too heavy.

### D — Fetch `/apps/` and `/games/` rendered DOM
Fragile, slow, semantically backward. Reject.

### E — Add a shared universal discovery registry consumed by homepage/apps/games
Architecturally cleanest long-term, but too invasive while those catalogs are concurrently dirty. Defer unless direct imports prove impossible.

## Phase-one winner

Architecture B: preserve the existing core `WORLD_CATALOG`, import `PUBLIC_APPS` and `GAMES`, normalize them into lightweight launcher records, and render grouped retractable sections. Catalog completeness remains independently testable.
